As a service provider we are responsible under § 7 (1) DDG for our own content on these pages under the general laws. Under §§ 8 to 10 DDG we are not obliged, as a service provider, to monitor transmitted or stored third-party information, or to investigate circumstances that point to unlawful activity.
legal.links.p: Our offering contains links to external third-party websites whose contents we have no influence over. We can therefore give no guarantee for that third-party content. The respective provider or operator of the linked pages is always responsible for their contents.
legal.about.p: vriltrainer is a public forced-choice experiment in remote viewing. The expected hit rate is 12.5 % — pure guessing. Ranks, titles and illustrations are satire on the relevant mythology and are not a claim about reality.
legal.licence.p: The source code is under the {START_LINK} AGPL-3.0-or-later {CLOSE_LINK}. Anyone running a modified version has to publish their changes — for a service whose entire promise is verifiability, that is not a formality.

proof.title: Proof
proof.eyebrow: The full derivation, computed in your browser
proof.h.pool: Which pool it is computed against
proof.pool.lead: The derivation draws against {START_EMPHASISED_TEXT}indices{CLOSE_EMPHASISED_TEXT} in the manifest. A different manifest yields different images from the same seed — which is why it is rehashed here and compared with the hash that already came with the coordinate.
proof.hashed.lead: Every field is length-prefixed so the boundaries are unambiguous: {START_TAG_CODE}framed(p₀, p₁, …) = SHA-256( LE64(|p₀|) ‖ p₀ ‖ LE64(|p₁|) ‖ p₁ ‖ … ){CLOSE_TAG_CODE} Without it, {START_TAG_CODE}("ab","c"){CLOSE_TAG_CODE} and {START_TAG_CODE}("a","bc"){CLOSE_TAG_CODE} hash alike.
proof.preimage.commitment: The full preimage string, {INTERPOLATION} bytes — exactly these bytes go into SHA-256:
proof.matches: Identical. The target was fixed before you chose.
proof.mismatch: Does not match. That would be a reason not to believe this site.
proof.h.seed: How the seed became the eight images
proof.keystream: The seed produces the keystream {START_TAG_CODE}block(i) = SHA-256( seed ‖ LE64(i) ){CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, read as 64-bit words little-endian. From it, in this order:
proof.independence: Computed with an implementation written independently of the server's. Both are checked against the same test vectors — that is the point: a check using the server's own code checks nothing. The computation runs in the browser; an independent third-party verifier does not exist in this version yet.
proof.manifestFailed: The pool manifest for this session could not be loaded. Without the list of images in exactly the published order there is nothing to recompute — and an empty proof panel would look like a test that passed.
proof.manifest.rehash: The recomputed hash of the manifest differs from the one it names itself.
proof.manifest.mismatch: The manifest delivered is not the one this session was fixed against.
proof.manifest.ok: {images} images in {categories} categories, hash recomputed and identical to the one already delivered with the coordinate.
proof.check.seal.ok: The values now disclosed produce exactly the number that stood on screen before your choice.
proof.check.seal.bad: The number from before cannot be reproduced from the disclosed values.
proof.check.echo.ok: The 32 bytes from your browser come back unchanged — the seed has two sides.
proof.check.echo.bad: The server returns different 32 bytes than your browser sent.
proof.check.draw.ok: The seed produces exactly these eight images, in exactly this order.
proof.check.draw.bad: The seed produces a different selection or a different order than the one shown.
proof.check.draw.error: The derivation did not run through: {reason}
proof.check.target.none: Without a derivation there is no recomputed target.
proof.check.target.ok: The recomputed target is the same one your choice was scored against.
proof.check.target.bad: The recomputed target is a different one from the one scored.
proof.note.echoed: 32 bytes from your browser, returned unchanged by the server
proof.note.notEchoed: 32 bytes from the server — your browser had sent {sent}
proof.note.overSorted: Over the sorted (id, category) pairs, categories first
proof.note.uniform: Uniform over the eight, independent of category size
proof.note.displayOrder: Descending Fisher-Yates; position {position} shows the target. {shown} images were shown.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.lead: This site stores as little as it can. What it does store is all of it, here.
privacy.short.1: No tracking, no cookies, no advertising, nothing passed on to advertisers.
privacy.short.2: No e-mail address, no password, no legal name — you choose what you are called.
privacy.short.3: The public record {START_TAG_STRONG}never carries your name{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}, only a random identifier.
privacy.short.4: You can delete your name at any time. Your sessions stay — why, is further down.
privacy.who.p: The person named in the {START_LINK}legal notice{CLOSE_LINK}, where the address and contact details are.
privacy.what.account: {START_TAG_STRONG}For your account:{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} the name you give yourself, a random public identifier, and a check value derived from your access link. The link itself is not stored — we could not restore your account even if we wanted to.
privacy.what.trials: {START_TAG_STRONG}For every session:{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} the time, the coordinate, the commitment to the target, the image you picked, the target, and whether it was a hit. That is the record this site makes publicly checkable.
privacy.what.logs: {START_TAG_STRONG}When you visit:{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} the web server logs your IP address, the time and the address requested. The service itself logs {START_EMPHASISED_TEXT}no{CLOSE_EMPHASISED_TEXT} IP address — only a request id, a method and a path, and the access link is cut off before anything is written.
privacy.public.p: The leaderboard shows your name and your public identifier. The downloadable record shows only the identifier — your name appears nowhere in it. A new name is published only after a human has reviewed it; until then public pages show a mask.
privacy.why.p: Account and sessions: Article 6(1)(b) GDPR — without them there is no service for you to use. Access logs: Article 6(1)(f) — a server that cannot see its own requests can neither be operated nor defended against abuse.
privacy.keep.1: {START_TAG_STRONG}An account that never played a session:{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} deleted automatically after 30 days, name and identifier with it.
privacy.keep.2: {START_TAG_STRONG}The web server's access log:{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} 7 days, then it is overwritten.
privacy.keep.3: {START_TAG_STRONG}Sessions in the public record:{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} permanently. The next section says why.
privacy.erase.name: {START_TAG_STRONG}You can delete your name at any time{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}, from the menu behind your name at the top. After that only the identifier stands in its place everywhere. It takes effect immediately and cannot be undone.
privacy.erase.trials: {START_TAG_STRONG}The sessions themselves cannot be deleted{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}, and that is the heart of this site: the record is a chain in which every entry secures the one before it. An entry that could be taken out would void the promise every other entry makes — the site could no longer show that the target was fixed before you chose. That is why the chain carries no name in the first place, only a random identifier. Once the name is deleted the record is still checkable, and belongs to nobody.
privacy.erase.rest: If you sign out without having saved your link, nobody can reach the account again — us included.
privacy.others.p: The server is hosted by Hetzner Online GmbH in Germany. In front of it sits Cloudflare, which forwards the traffic and processes IP addresses in doing so; this can involve transfers to third countries. There are no other recipients — no analytics, no ad networks, no social networks.
privacy.cookies.p: None. Your access link is kept in your browser's local storage so that you are still signed in after a reload — technically necessary, which is why this site does not ask your permission for it. Signing out deletes it.
privacy.rights.p: You have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and objection. For access you need not apply for anything: the complete record for your identifier is in the log you can download at the foot of every page. For anything else, a message to the address in the legal notice is enough. You may also complain to a data protection supervisory authority.
privacy.dsa.p: The only content users publish here is their display name. If one strikes you as illegal, report it to the address in the legal notice — that is the point of contact under Article 16 of the Digital Services Act. Give the name or the public identifier and say in one sentence what the problem is. You will get an answer, and if the report is justified the name is removed. Names are reviewed by a human before publication in any case.
privacy.note.p: A public experiment. Pure guessing hits 12.5 % of the time, and that is the expected result. The site claims nothing else and proves nobody psychic — it works out whether the numbers depart from chance, and publishes everything needed to check.
erase.confirm: The name is removed immediately and cannot be restored. Your sessions stay in the record — under your identifier, without a name.
erase.failed: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
